title: Minestra di Pasta e Patate
subtitle: Italian potato and pasta soup
excerpt: A thick, filling Neapolitan soup of potato and small pasta cooked together until the potato breaks apart and thickens the broth. Topped with parmesan and a drizzle of good olive oil.
sourceNotes: Neapolitan cucina povera; pasta e patate is one of the great simple soups of southern Italy.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a large pot and reheat with a little extra water, as the pasta absorbs liquid as it sits.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the potato soup base ahead. Add the pasta only when reheating so it does not go soft.

content.text: This is a classic Neapolitan soup of potato and pasta. It is thick, almost porridge-like when done right. Use any small pasta shape you have. Add more water if you want it soupier.

items.prepNote: small shape such as tubetti or ditalini

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and rosemary if using. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the potato and stir to coat. Pour in the passata and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Use the back of a spoon to break apart roughly a third of the potato in the pan. This thickens the soup without making it smooth.
Add the pasta. Cook for the time on the packet, stirring often so it does not stick. Add a little water if the soup becomes too thick.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve in bowls with a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil, black pepper, and grated parmesan.

items.symptom: The pasta has gone soft and the soup is stodgy.
items.cause: The pasta was cooked too far ahead or sat in the hot soup for too long.
items.fix: Cook pasta to just short of tender before serving. If reheating leftovers, add fresh pasta to the reheated base.

items.symptom: The soup is thin and watery.
items.cause: Not enough potato was broken down to thicken the broth.
items.fix: Mash more of the potato into the broth and simmer uncovered for a few extra minutes.

items.symptom: The soup has caught on the bottom.
items.cause: The heat was too high once the pasta was added.
items.fix: Stir frequently once pasta goes in, and keep the heat at a gentle simmer.
